text:
maria: Heads up — we just started seeing a sharp spike of GPU OOMs in prod after the kernel-selector rollout at 06:12 UTC. Affected pods show KV cache pressure + workspace allocations climbing.
sam: saw it in the dashboard. 99th latency fine but memory climbs until OOM. nvml logs show fragmented allocations.
lee: any idea which kernel variant triggered it? autotune or new matmul kernel?
maria: autotune + new continuous-batching heuristic enabled. Profiling (quick) shows extra peak allocations when batching aligns with long-prefix chat requests. KV cache keeps hot prefixes and isn't evicting fast enough.
ryan: timeline: rollout -> kernel A selected for long sequences -> larger workspace chosen -> KV TTL not reduced -> memory rises -> OOMs.
ops-oncall: triage checklist? we need mitigations we can apply ASAP.
maria: immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
  1) disable kernel-autotune at runtime to force fallback to previous kernel:

```
export RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_AUTOTUNE=0
# or set via configmap: runtime.kernel.autotune: false
kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/runtime RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_AUTOTUNE=0
```

  2) lower max_batch_size for the model route to reduce peak workspace sizing:

```
redwood route update --name chat-v2 --max-batch-size=8
```

  3) enable short-circuit fallback to smaller-model variant (quantized) for requests > 1024 tokens:

```
runtime.route.rules:
  - if: request.length > 1024
    then: route: chat-v2-quantized
```

  4) force KV cache soft-eviction by lowering TTL and reducing per-key keepers:

```
kvcache.default_ttl_seconds=30
kvcache.target_eviction_rate=0.2
```

  5) enable buffer-reuse mode to reduce transient allocations (best-effort):

```
runtime.gpu.buffer_reuse=true
```

sam: good. For rollback path: we can pin the image to the pre-rollout tag if disabling autotune doesn't fully mitigate.
lee: do we have a one-line script to flip everything? ops, can you run it?
ops-oncall: running now — will post results.
deploy-bot: @maria started rollout revert: image runtime:v2026-rc4 -> runtime:v2026-rc3
ops-oncall: kube env updated, kernel_autotune=0, buffer_reuse enabled, max_batch_size set to 8. Applying KV TTL patch.
ryan: monitoring — memory curve already flattening on node group A :eyes:
maria: good, keep watch. Next: follow-up tasks for next day:
  - telemetry: add a per-kernel workspace histogram and per-prefix KV residency gauge
  - add a circuit-breaker rule that rejects >X concurrent long-prefix requests per-pod
  - tighten batching heuristic: prefer batch alignment windows when prefix length < 512
  - add automated rollback when OOM rate > 0.5% over 5m
sam: plus a test harness: replay production traces with new kernel profile and KV config in staging.
lee: I'll open a PR with kernel selector safe-guards (max_workspace_bytes cap + conservative fallback on fragmentation).
maria: quick note on debugging commands used:
```
nvidia-smi dmon -s u
kubectl logs -n redwood runtime-pod-abc -c runtime --since=2m | grep OOM
curl https://telemetry.internal/api/v1/query?metric=runtime_gpu_workspace_bytes&range=5m
```

ops-oncall: after fixes, deploy-bot reports rollout revert completed and pods are stable.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: runtime -> v2026-rc3 :white_check_mark:
ryan: memory OOM alerts dropped to zero in the last 3m.
maria: retrospective action items: add a short playbook doc (operational steps + exact flags) and a small canary run for kernel-selector changes. Also schedule an eval run comparing quantized fallback quality.
sam: thanks everyone. please add any logs to the incident ticket #INC-8421 and tag me.
lee: adding a unit test for allocator soft-reserve under fragmented allocations.
ops-oncall: closing active paged incident channel once CI checks pass and no OOMs for 15m.
ryan: :thumbsup:
